title: Two riders.
paragraphs: You won’t notice the difference at first.
Because deception doesn’t come wearing darkness.
And your heart—if you’re honest—has already followed voices that felt right… but led you wrong.
And now you’re standing in the tension between what feels good… and what is actually God.
“I looked, and behold, a white horse! And its rider had a bow… and he went out conquering, and to conquer.”
“Then I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse! The one sitting on it is called Faithful and True… and in righteousness he judges and makes war.”
Some scholars interpret the first rider as a symbol of deception—false peace, counterfeit authority, a power that looks righteous but isn’t rooted in Christ.
Not everything that wins… is from God.
Not everything that prospers… is holy.
Not everything that feels peaceful… is truth.
Because sin rarely announces itself as destruction.
Until one day, you wake up and realize…
You’ve been following the wrong rider.
And now it owns space in your soul.
“But each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death.”
It can look clean on the outside.
You can still go to church.
While something inside you is quietly drifting away from God.
That’s the rider with the bow.
“He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and the name by which he is called is The Word of God.”
The same One who hung on a cross—
Every secret you thought no one saw.
“Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.”
Every moment you thought you got away with it—
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
While you were still in it.
Not permission to stay the same—
Because the Gospel is not behavior modification.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
You don’t have to live divided anymore.
You don’t have to keep managing a double life.
You don’t have to keep pretending.
The easier it is to normalize what’s destroying you.
And the harder it becomes to hear the voice of the true King.
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.”
The one that feeds your flesh?
Or the One who died for your soul?
Because only one Rider leads to life.
Only one walked out of the grave.
And He’s not asking for perfection.
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
That’s what the true Rider offers.
